SimWorkshopPage.title: Sim workshop
SimWorkshopPage.subtitle: Describe a simulation and build it together with the assistant. Every version is checked and kept here, so you can compare, go back and download.
SimWorkshopPage.empty: No drafts yet. Open the assistant and describe the simulation you want: what students should do and measure, the level, and the quantity they should work out themselves.
SimWorkshopPage.levelHelp: Level 3 means the sim is valid, runs, fits the screen and talks to the tutor. It does NOT mean the physics is right — that is for you to check.
SimWorkshopPage.noScreenshots: No screenshots for this version: the browser check did not run.
SimWorkshopPage.draftOnly: Drafts are visible only to you. Publishing to your classes comes in a later version.
SimWorkshopPage.assistantPlaceholder: Describe a simulation, or what to change
SimWorkshopPage.assistantEmpty: Describe the simulation you want. For example: “A four-stroke engine cut in half, with a p-V diagram. Students vary the compression ratio and measure heat and work for one cycle; they work out the efficiency themselves.”
SimWorkshopPage.unavailable: The Sim workshop is not switched on in this environment yet.
SimWorkshopPage.lockedHeading: Not switched on for you yet
SimWorkshopPage.lockedBody: The Sim workshop lets you describe a simulation and build it with an assistant, checking every version. It is switched on per teacher by a researcher on the project. Ask, and they can turn it on for you.
SimWorkshopPage.lockedAsk: Ask to have it switched on
SimWorkshopPage.previewUnavailable: No sandbox is configured in this environment, so the live preview cannot run. The screenshots below still show each version.
SimWorkshopPage.previewPlaceholder: Your simulation appears here as soon as the assistant has checked its first version. Describe it in the assistant panel.
